feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and good platform/analytics depth. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level leadership with strong alignment to the headline positioning.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Strong breadth across strategy, governance, web platforms, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search, making the profile distinctive.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and dilute impact. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and earlier NACo roles: e.g., adoption, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and list punctuation around “web, email, social, and multimedia” (serial comma usage varies). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language like “leading” or “delivering” to sharpen executive tone.
- Add one high-value proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Tighten the list of capabilities to avoid sounding like a skills dump; group related items under “web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations.”
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivered large-scale platform and editorial transformation, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views, while advancing multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Digital leader” is close to the subtitle; use the intro to add evidence, not repeat positioning.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths and reduce generic items like “Multi-channel communications operations.”
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, swap one broad item for a more differentiated capability such as “Drupal-based platform strategy” or “Cross-channel content systems leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences,” governance, analytics, and multimedia are already reinforced in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make the footer feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and specifics where possible: e.g., “launched,” “scaled,” “supported campaign growth,” “improved policy-content discovery.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent serial commas.
- Consider this tighter version: “Selected recent projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy-content discovery. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future growth…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may be the best differentiator because it adds a distinct cross-channel example not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and distinguish it from the NACo roles by emphasizing consulting scope, AI search, and enterprise web improvement.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise web strategy, campaign delivery, content operations, and digital governance.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one impact-led line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make Drupal work outcome-focused: “Designed and launched modular Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Recast technical/AI bullets for seniority: “Led enterprise web enhancements, CMS/front-end troubleshooting, and an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if possible: launch dates, traffic, adoption, time saved, or number of teams/users supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current phrasing overlaps heavily with NACo on governance, analytics, and multi-channel operations.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may undersell seniority unless balanced with strategy/leadership.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be sharper by foregrounding the biggest outcomes, tightening channel-management language, and avoiding overlap with earlier NACo roles on newsletters/video/editorial coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the strongest achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight outcome-focused; add metrics if available: email growth, engagement rates, social growth, video output, cost savings, or production turnaround.
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built analytics and publishing systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery; established governance, standards, and cross-department workflows to improve reporting and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Managed newsletters/video/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2018–2022 NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- The in-house studio bullet may overlap with the footer’s Advocacy Video Series project; emphasize organizational capability-building here, not recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to operational leadership and channel growth during 2018–2022, with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale/results: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with stronger operational language: “Built cross-functional editorial planning processes and standardized digital publishing workflows, improving coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet; keep this version focused on execution, not enterprise governance.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered content strategy and campaign planning
- Consider dropping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” unless messaging is a target-role keyword; it reads less differentiated than governance/operations leadership.
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid vague terms like “focused”; “audience-centered” or “user-centered” is cleaner.
- If space allows, add one scope cue in the section intro elsewhere, e.g., “enterprise” or “organization-wide,” to reinforce seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with multiple NACo bullets on editorial planning and storytelling.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and CMS modernization” instead of listing platforms first.
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths from current/NACo work: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Trim lower-signal or older items unless job-relevant; move WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable to Technical + IT if space is tight.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or more technical here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g. “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI reporting” instead of listing tools separately.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support” for stronger phrasing.
- Tighten “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion performance analysis” only if accurate; otherwise keep “SEO and web performance analysis.”
- Suggested version: “- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework design and executive dashboards - SEO and web performance analysis - Insight generation for content, UX and campaign optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every tool here if the Technical + IT section already carries the full stack.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery environment and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Broadcast, Studio & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and studio system operation
- Virtual event technical direction and show flow coordination
- If accurate, add scale/outcome language instead of generic terms, e.g. “multi-camera livestream delivery” or “in-house studio production for advocacy and event programming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is already reinforced by work history and Technical + IT tools; avoid overexplaining it here.
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies wording; broaden this item to studio/event operations to add new value.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In this section, make it more specific and weighted toward the platforms most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show level/use: **Drupal (enterprise CMS, migration, microsites) • WordPress (site administration) • SharePoint (intranet/content management) • Power Pages (Microsoft web apps) • GitHub Pages (static sites)**
- If space allows, emphasize strongest platform: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise publishing for 50+ users)** and keep others shorter.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- If Drupal is already prominent in recent experience and projects, use this item to add proficiency/context rather than restating names only.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broader platform skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome signals tied to recent work: e.g., “front-end implementation for Drupal microsites,” “serverless scripts,” or “deployment automation.”
- Consider grouping by function for readability: “Front-end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery | Integrations/ops: APIs, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- If space is tight, keep the detailed tools here and trim the overlapping Topline Skills entry to broader categories only.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more selective and grouped around systems you’ve recently used to drive operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/recency and group by function: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Drop lower-signal or older tools unless they were central recently: Basecamp, Trello
- If space allows, add light context instead of only listing tools, e.g. “Airtable workflow systems • Power Automate/Zapier integrations • Jira/Asana project operations • Slack/Teams collaboration”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis here without adding specificity.
- Slack and Teams are collaboration tools, not automation systems; separating them improves precision.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. This section should signal level of ownership and enterprise use, not just list tools—especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email, Marketing Automation & Community Platforms
- Tighten and modernize the line: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals to show use case, e.g. Higher Logic (member communications/community) • Dynamics 365 CI/Journeys (segmentation, journeys, campaign ops)
- Only keep platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light/older exposure, move it to “Additional Tools” or drop it

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in Work Experience; avoid restating outcomes here unless tied to platform-specific capability.
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Tighten it into a cleaner technical stack and use broader labels that support the stronger impact already shown in recent NACo work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing) • KPI/dashboard reporting
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI/dashboard reporting” to sound more outcome-oriented and less generic.
- Use “SEO analysis” instead of just “SEO” to keep this item focused on analytics/optimization rather than broader marketing.
- If space allows elsewhere, move measurable impact to recent roles instead of here, e.g., analytics stack supporting 3.5M annual page views and leadership reporting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping the fuller version in one place only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating too many adjacent terms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since strategy/leadership are already covered in more recent entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving production workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s day-to-day work.”
- If metrics exist, replace “high-impact” with specifics such as views, engagement, event count, or reduced reliance on vendors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; specify what changed operationally.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim broad language about “supporting programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Add the standout digital contribution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support research dissemination and member communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes launched, audience reached, teams supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/innovation support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating video, livestream, or broader digital operations language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool proficiency only.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
